title: Avoid using PATCH requests for web routes
description:
Browser forms do not support PATCH, so you need to use javascript. Switching to POST for web routes avoids the need to javascript and makes the specs simpler, since you can use the normal Capybara API.

I previously handled similar cases using `r.api_patch_web_post`, but that is an ugly name, and this behavior will extend to all future web routes, so it makes sense to change the default `r.patch` behavior. This updates the two `r.api_patch_web_post` calls to use `r.patch`.

While removing the javascript code, I noticed I neglected to remove the inline-edit javascript in a6a8b8b5edc63cbcb2e80cba20346b29e9450f71, so this includes a commit to remove that.

Best viewed ignoring whitespace differences.

title: Convert web routes to use POST instead of DELETE
description:
This allows all deletion routes to work correctly without
javascript. It significantly simplifies the specs, since they
can use normal Capybara methods instead of page.driver.delete.
This uses the same approach previous used for r.patch.

The second commit is quite large because of how many r.delete
routes we have. I would have liked to split it up, but many parts
are interdependent, and I don't think it's possible if we want the
intermediate commits to pass specs. I tried to do as much possible
work in the first commit, which reorganizes routes without
changing behavior

Here's a breakdown of the different parts:

In helpers/general.rb, override r.delete to operate similarly
to r.patch, where for web routes, it matches POST with an
additional delete segment.

In the routes, for web deletion requests, use r.redirect.
Add flash notices in all places they were missed. Add
handle validation failures in routes that can fail (maybe it
should be added in additional, currently untested cases?).

Special handling for specific routes:

* inference_api_key: Use check_found_object to avoid multiple
  conditionals.

* postgres: For metric destination deletion, mark that no audit log is
  expected if the metric destination does not exist.

* private_location: Update the route structure changes, missed in the
  previous commit.

Change the delete_button component. Drop the csrf_url, redirect, and
method arguments, no longer needed. Add the following optional
arguments:

* exact_url: Set to not append /delete to the URL, used by the private
  subnet disconnect template.

* form_id: Sets the form attribute on the button, associated it with a
  different form than the default one. Used in the token template.
  When this is used, it only adds the button tag, it does not wrap it
  in a form tag.

* icon: Override the icon used. Used in the github runner template.

* hidden_inputs: Use the given hidden inputs in the form. Used in the
  billing template.

* attributes: Customize the attributes used. Used in multiple
  templates.

Most other templates modified in this commit modify only the arguments
passed to the delete_button component, and in most cases, there are
fewer arguments. Some templates needed special handling:

* github runners: Switch from using the button template to the delete
  button component. Inline the destroy_url variable, since it is only
  needed once and not twice.

* users: Add separate form tags for each user and invitations, and
  use the form_id argument to associat the button to those forms. This
  wasn't needed before as javascript was used for submission, but it
  is needed now, as the buttons would otherwise submit the containing
  form (which is used for updating user permissions.

Specs were partially updated by Claude with the following prompt:

```
In the previous commit, I made changes to use the HTTP POST
method instead of the DELETE method for deletion requests from web
browsers. This is to avoid the need to use javascript to submit the
requests. This results in 58 spec failures, which you can see in
`spec.log`. Please update each failing spec to use standard Capybara
testing methods such as `click_button`, instead of the current code
that uses `page.driver.delete`. When updating the specs, always
check for for the expected flash notice using `expect(page).to
have_flash_notice`, and remove any comments related to using
javascript for delete requests.
```

This reduced the number of failing specs from 58 to 33. Remaining
specs were fixed manually, and even in those cases Claude helped
with the cleanup even if it didn't fix the issue completely. This
reduces and simplifies most of the related specs.

Delete a bunch of code from the .delete-btn click function in the
javascript, as it is no longer used.

Best viewed ignoring whitespace.

>   - **Components**:

title: Remove unused association methods
description:
Such methods consume unnecessary memory, resulting in longer full garbage collections.

This uses Sequel's unused_associations plugin to detect the unused associations. Unfortunately, there are a number of false positives, due to mocking in the specs. I've flagged those associations so they aren't considered unused, but such flags should be removed after the unnecessary mocking is removed from the specs (and association mocking should always be considered unnecessary).

This runs the unused associations check in CI, so that code will fail CI if it introduces an unused association, or stops using a currently used association without removing it or removing the unused association methods.

title: Add VM host health check to verify clock source is tsc
description:
tsc is the preferred clock source because it is more reliable and precise. Our hosts use tsc by default, but in some cases they may fall back to hpet if issues are detected with tsc.

When a host switches to hpet, it can cause instability and runtime issues for runners. In particular, this leads to errors like "OS monotonic time stepped backwards!", which we've observed frequently in Elixir-based workflow jobs.

We should monitor the clock source on VM hosts and alert if any host switches from tsc to hpet, so we can take corrective action early.

title: Add retry logic when instance is unsupported in the AZ
description:
When AWS returns an Unsupported error during instance creation, it typically means the requested instance type is not available in the current availability zone. Previously, this would cause provisioning to fail and get stuck.

This change adds retry logic that:
- Catches Unsupported errors during instance creation
- Excludes the failed availability zone from future attempts
- Recreates the NIC in a different AZ using the exclusion list
- Limits retries to 5 attempts to prevent infinite loops
- Logs retry attempts for observability

The implementation introduces two new state machine labels: wait_old_nic_deleted waits for the old NIC to be fully deleted before creating a new one, preventing resource conflicts. wait_nic_recreated waits for the new NIC to be ready before retrying instance creation.

The retry state (count, excluded AZs, and subnet ID) is preserved in the strand stack to survive across state transitions.

fixes https://linear.app/ubicloud/issue/UBI-252/implement-az-changeretry-in-case-of-capacity-issues

title: Make PageNexus.assemble upsert existing Pages instead of ignoring them
description:
Previously, when PageNexus.assemble was called with tag_parts that matched an existing active Page, it would simply return early and ignore the new data. This meant that updates to page summaries, details, or severity would be lost.

Now, when an existing active Page is found by tag, it gets updated with the new summary, details, and severity. This ensures Pages always reflect the most current state.

title: Update Util.exception_to_hash
description:
This makes two changes to Util.exception.to_hash:

* It adds an into keyword argument. This will add the :exception
  key to that hash instead of always using a new hash. For backwards
  compatibility, the default is a new empty hash.

* It uses an array to hold the exception information. If backtraces are
  being logged (the default), it includes all exception causes in the
  array.

This switches callers of the form:

```ruby
{...}.merge(Util.exception_to_hash(ex))
```

to:

```ruby
Util.exception_to_hash(ex, into: {...})
```

Which eliminates 2 hash allocations per call (as merge returns a new
hash).

This also removes the loop in the dispatcher to emit each exception
cause as a separate log entry, since now the single log entry includes
all causes.

This builds on top of #4446.

title: [destroying #5] Use destroying label in before_run
description:
We now rely on the destroying semaphore to prevent multiple hops to the destroy label.

Most duplicated before_run logic has already been moved to the base prog. For the remaining cases, we can use the destroying semaphore instead of checking labels directly.

title: Allow specifying private subnet name when creating PostgreSQL database in the API/CLI
description:
This makes things simpler for the API/CLI user. Before, they could rename the created private subnet, but doing so requires knowing the ubid of the created postgres resource, which makes it more challenging to script. This allows for specifying the name up front, so that after creation, you can add firewalls directly to it without parsing the output from other requests/commands.

Mostly written by Claude Code using the following prompt:

```
Add support for accepting a private subnet name when creating a
postgres resource

* Update assemble in prog/postgres/postgres_resource_nexus.rb to
  accept private subnet name
* Update helpers/postgres.rb to pass private subnet name when calling
  subnet name, for api requests and not web resources.
* Update openapi/openapi.yml to accept private subnet name when
  creating a postgres database
* Update cli-commands/pg/post/create.rb to accept an option to specify
  the private subnet name
* Update spec/routes/api/cli/pg/create_spec.rb to pass the option to
  specify the private subnet name, and check that the created private
  subnet has that name.
```

I changed the CLI option from `-n` to `-P`, and did some minor refactoring.

title: [destroying #6] Add before_destroy callback to Prog::Base
description:
- **Move Prog::Test2 to a separate file**

Prog::Test2 was in the same file as Prog::Test and inherited from it.

In real progs, we don't use inheritance, and this setup caused
unexpected behavior. For example, it inherited hop_destroy method, but
since @labels is empty, it can't hop there.

It's better to keep it in a separate file and mimic the structure of
real progs.

- **Add before_destroy callback to Prog::Base**

Some progs run cleanup logic (like finalizing billing records) in before_run, but this logic only needs to execute once before hopping to destroy.

The before_destroy runs exactly once before the destroy hop, avoiding the need to duplicate the entire before_run logic.

title: Observe archival backlog and page if it exceeds threshold (try 2)
description: Add an SSH call to count the number of WAL files ready to be archived and raise a Page if it exceeds a threshold. In the previous attempt, this was added to pulse_check, which caused a problem. Since postgres server pulse checks require an event loop, running exec! on the same session is not safe, and can cause state corruption which lead to stuck SSH sessions. In this attempt, we move the backlog check to the metrics export path.

title: Remove unnecessary association options
description:
These are detected by the new detect_unnecessary_association_options Sequel plugin.

The first commit also fixes association types for a couple InferenceEndpoint associations.

title: Nap when nic is still attached at destroy
description:
## Register deadline to prevent indefinite NIC destroy retries
Add a 5-minute deadline when entering the destroy flow to ensure
the cleanup process does not hang indefinitely during retry loops.
This prevents resource leaks when transient errors persist longer
than expected.

## Skip NIC deletion when AWS resource not yet created
When destroy is triggered before the NIC AWS resource entity has been
created (e.g., early failure in provisioning), skip directly to
destroy_entities to clean up database records without attempting AWS
API calls that would fail.

## Retry network interface deletion when in use
Network interface deletion can fail with "currently in use" when the
underlying VM is still detaching. This typically occurs during
concurrent VM and NIC cleanup operations.

Add retry logic to handle this transient state by napping for 5
seconds when encountering this specific error. Other deletion errors
are still raised immediately. The deadline registered in before_run
prevents indefinite retries.

## Retry security group deletion when in use

title: Add uuid type to config for earlier validation
Update openssl from 3.3.2 to 4.0.0
description:
First rubocop fails with the following error:

    lib/util.rb:29:3: W: Lint/ShadowedException: Do not shadow rescued Exceptions.
      rescue OpenSSL::PKey::ECError, OpenSSL::PKey::DSAError ...
      ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

It's starting to complain about because errors are unified under OpenSSL::PKey::PKeyError at https://github.com/ruby/openssl/pull/929

So no need to rescue specific errors anymore, we can just rescue the parent error.

Secondly, postgres_resource_nexus_spec test fails with the following error:

    1) Prog::Postgres::PostgresResourceNexus#refresh_certificates rotates server certificate using root_cert_2 if root_cert_1 is close to expiration
       Failure/Error: expect { nx.refresh_certificates }.to hop("wait")

       ArgumentError:
         OpenSSL::PKey::EC.new cannot be called without arguments; pkeys are immutable with OpenSSL 3.0
       # ./prog/postgres/postgres_resource_nexus.rb:305:in 'OpenSSL::PKey::EC#initialize'
       # ./prog/postgres/postgres_resource_nexus.rb:305:in 'Class#new'
       # ./prog/postgres/postgres_resource_nexus.rb:305:in 'Prog::Postgres::PostgresResourceNexus#create_certificate'
       # ./prog/postgres/postgres_resource_nexus.rb:187:in 'Prog::Postgres::PostgresResourceNexus#refresh_certificates'
       # ./spec/prog/postgres/postgres_resource_nexus_spec.rb:324:in 'block (4 levels) in <top (required)>'
       # ./spec/spec_helper.rb:173:in 'block (3 levels) in <top (required)>'
       # ./spec/prog/postgres/postgres_resource_nexus_spec.rb:324:in 'block (3 levels) in <top (required)>'
       # ./spec/spec_helper.rb:62:in 'block (3 levels) in <top (required)>'
       # ./spec/spec_helper.rb:61:in 'block (2 levels) in <top (required)>'

It doesn't allow to pass nil to OpenSSL::PKey::EC.new anymore.

title: Remove LocationCredential project association
description:
This association was broken, as the location_credential table does not have a project_id column. This resulted in a production exception:

NoMethodError - undefined method 'project_id' for an instance of LocationCredential

description: This was already approved in #4364, but it got merged into #4363, then lost in a rebase.

title: Demock postgres_server_nexus_spec
description:
Replace 32 instance_double mocks with real PostgresServer, PostgresResource, PostgresTimeline, and Vm objects. Add helper methods create_postgres_timeline, create_postgres_resource, create_read_replica_resource, create_postgres_server, and create_standby_nexus to encapsulate fixture creation. Reduces receive() stubs from 365 to 222 by using real object associations.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Demock update_firewall_rules_spec
description:
Replace instance_double mocks with real persisted Vm, Firewall, Nic, LoadBalancer, and other models, letting Sequel handle all relationships.

Ref: clover-mol-cvd5

title: Add admin page to find VMs by IPv4 address
description: Investigating abuse reports requires finding VMs associated with specific IP addresses. Previously, this required using pry for active VMs and direct database queries for archived ones. This commit adds a custom admin page at /custom/vm_by_ipv4 that searches both active VMs and archived records from the last 15 days in a single query. The page accepts comma-separated IP addresses and displays matching VMs with their metadata including project, boot image, and archive timestamp. The implementation also introduces a generic custom views system that automatically discovers ERB templates in views/admin/customs/. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Update paradedb image to have wal-g service file
description: https://github.com/ubicloud/paradedb-postgres-images/pull/3

title: Fix Clog related flaky test in vpc_nexus_spec.rb
description: Since subnet creation may generate an extra log regarding a disallowed subnet selection, checking the Clog emit caused a flaky test. We're adding an allow statement for such a case.

title: Introduce config to limit SSH IP access
description: Particularly necessary in environments barring open SSH access

title: Fix sha256 of postgres_paradedb image
description:
In commit dba7160e88117d3f104b79be463d7b690b00f60a we made a mistake and created an image from the old code with a new version. The image is updated now and has a new sha256.

sha is visible here https://github.com/ubicloud/paradedb-postgres-images/actions/runs/20786470863/job/59701267749

title: Fix double nested exception logs
description:
`Util.exception_to_hash` already returns a hash with an exception key, so wrapping it again with another exception key is unnecessary and results in double nesting.

When rebasing #4465, I missed some changes in #4446. This includes the changes in #4446 that were not already merged as part of #4465.

title: Don't base64 decode KMS key, as KMS key is already base64
Add Sshable#write_file and use it
description: This method implements a common pattern used for writing files over SSH, using tee path > /dev/null with the content on stdin.

title: Add more tables to admin panel
description:
- **Use admin table component for existing tables**
  

- **Convert billing info Stripe data from raw JSON to table**
  The raw JSON format was difficult to read and inconsistent with the page
  layout. Displaying it as a table improves readability and visual
  alignment.
  
  Since some billing info records may not have Stripe data, the table
  component now supports nil values.
  

- **Display Stripe data for payment methods in the admin panel**
  

- **Remove unnecessary name alias in the admin panel**
  Since admin_label already falls back to ubid when the model doesn’t have
  a name, we can use admin_label directly without adding a separate alias
  for name.
  
  It's a more generic solution for the future models.
  

- **Add billing info table to admin panel**
  

- **Add payment method table to admin panel**

title: Fix wal-g service stale credentials issue when switching to new timeline
description: This is a bug we introduced when we started using wal-g service for wal pushing. When we switch to a new timeline, essentially we are changing the bucket we use in the backing store as well, however, wal-g service only reads the environment file at the startup time. Therefore, it was using old bucket related credentials and addresses. This commit fixes that behavior.

title: Avoid NoMethodError when viewing PG create page
description: If viewing the PG create page with flavor=lantern, if latern support was not enabled for the project, a NoMethodError was raised. Using postgres_flavors avoids the issue.

title: Allow Clog.emit to accept metadata as argument
description:
Previously, Clog.emit always yielded to the block to get metadata. This would make sense if the block was lazily-evaluated, or not always called. However, the block is eagerly evaluated and always called if given. It's more efficient to pass the metadata directly as an argument.

For the heavy lifting of fixing callers and specs, I used Claude Code. It did a pretty poor job fixing callers, and I had to refix most. It did what I asked to fix spec mocking, but what I asked was not nearly sufficient, so I had to fix most mocking manually as well.

This currently still allows a block. I did this to reduce problems when merging this with other in-flight PRs. No remaining code passes a block. After this is merged, I'll change Clog.emit to raise if passed a block and fix any newly introduced calls that pass a block.

title: Handle lsn_monitor being nil in PostgresServer#failover_target
description: Ran into this locally where lsn monitor wasn't being created because monitor wasn't running

title: Remove support for passing blocks to Clog.emit
description: To avoid the chance someone passes a block that is silently ignored, raise for this case (without this, Ruby would warn, but tests would still pass).

title: Add pg_config & pgbouncer_config to endpoints for creating read replicas
description: Also add tags to restore, which was previously added to read replica creation

title: Add constraint ensuring used_hugepages_1g >= 0
description: Over-deallocation bugs have occasionally caused used_hugepages_1g to go negative in production. Adding a database constraint catches these bugs at write time rather than when symptoms appear later. This mirrors the existing used_cores_above_zero constraint.

title: Add deleting display state to private subnet
description:
When we trigger the destroy action for a private subnet, it still appears as “available” until the very end of the process.

Adding a “deleting” state would make it clear that the resource is in the process of being destroyed.

Since this is the first semaphore dependent display state for private subnets, we need to load it eagerly.

title: Avoid inconsistency in e.g. usage in CLI
description: Always use "e.g." instead of mixing "e.g." and "e.g".

title: Make ubiblk the default storage backend for new hosts
description: Ubiblk has been tested in production and has been stable. This change makes it the default storage backend for new hosts.

title: Display current usage of project in the admin panel
description: - **Add space between object extra in the admin panel** - **Add collapsible table to admin table** Adding new extras to object detail pages makes them longer and harder to find relevant data. When I added current usage data to the project detail page, it became very long. To address this, I added the ability to collapse tables so the data is hidden by default and shown only when needed. This is implemented using the HTML details/summary elements, which is a pure CSS solution. title: Remove the use of :no_association_method association option
description:
The admin site expects that if an association exists, the association method exists. It's currently undertested, but it's likely all models that were using :no_association_method have broken admin pages (at least GitHubInstallation did).

Change the unused_associations_check rake task to not recommend the use of this option, as it currently doesn't recommend the use of :no_dataset_method.

title: Return 400 instead of 500 for invalid Kubernetes version
description: This commit adds proper validation for Kubernetes version parameter that makes the endpoint return a 400 Bad Request with helpful error message instead of throwing a 500.
